nodes.name: Estimation Problem (Wiener Problem)
nodes.statement: Given observed values $y(t_0), \ldots, y(t)$ where $y(t) = x_1(t) + x_2(t)$ (signal plus noise), determine an estimate $X_1(t_1|t)$ of $x_1(t_1)$. Subsumes filtering ($t_1 = t$), prediction ($t_1 > t$), and smoothing ($t_1 < t$).
nodes.statement_clean: Estimate the signal at time $t_1$ from noisy observations on $[t_0, t]$.

nodes.name: Loss function
nodes.statement: A loss function $L(\varepsilon)$ on the estimation error $\varepsilon = x_1(t_1) - X_1(t_1)$ satisfies $L(0)=0$, $L(\varepsilon_2) \geq L(\varepsilon_1) \geq 0$ when $\varepsilon_2 \geq \varepsilon_1 \geq 0$, and $L(\varepsilon) = L(-\varepsilon)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Symmetric, non-decreasing penalty on estimation error, vanishing at zero.

nodes.name: Risk (average loss)
nodes.statement: The risk is $E\{L[x_1(t_1) - X_1(t_1)]\}$, the expected value of the loss function evaluated at the estimation error.

nodes.name: Conditional probability distribution of estimate
nodes.statement: $F(\xi_1) = \Pr[x_1(t_1) \leq \xi_1 \mid y(t_0)=\eta(t_0), \ldots, y(t)=\eta(t)]$, summarising all information observations convey about $x_1(t_1)$.

nodes.name: Linear manifold $Y(t)$
nodes.statement: The vector space (linear manifold) $Y(t)$ of all linear combinations $\sum_{i=t_0}^{t} a_i y(i)$ of observed random variables, viewed as a finite-dimensional subspace of the space of observations.

nodes.name: Orthogonal random variables
nodes.statement: Two vectors $u, v \in Y(t)$ are orthogonal if $E uv = 0$.

nodes.name: Orthonormal basis in $Y(t)$
nodes.statement: A set $\{e_{t_0}, \ldots, e_t\} \subset Y(t)$ such that every vector in $Y(t)$ is uniquely expressible as a linear combination of the basis and $E e_i e_j = \delta_{ij}$.

nodes.name: Orthogonal projection $\bar{x}(t_1|t)$
nodes.statement: Any random variable $x$ decomposes uniquely as $x = \bar{x} + \tilde{x}$ where $\bar{x} = \sum_{i=t_0}^{t} (E x e_i) e_i \in Y(t)$ and $\tilde{x}$ is orthogonal to $Y(t)$. $\bar{x}$ is the orthogonal projection of $x$ on $Y(t)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Decomposition of a random variable into its $L^2$-projection onto the observation subspace and an orthogonal residual.

nodes.name: State of a dynamic system
nodes.statement: The state is the least amount of information about the past behavior of the system needed to predict its future behavior; dynamics is described in terms of state transitions.

nodes.name: Linear dynamic system (continuous)
nodes.statement: $dx/dt = F(t)x + D(t) u(t)$ with output $y(t) = M(t) x(t)$, where $x$ is the $n$-vector state, $u(t)$ the $m$-vector input ($m \leq n$), and $F(t), D(t), M(t)$ are matrices of compatible dimensions.

nodes.name: Transition matrix $\Phi(t+1; t)$
nodes.statement: For the discrete linear system $x(t+1) = \Phi(t+1; t) x(t) + \Delta(t) u(t)$, the matrix $\Phi(t_2; t_1)$ describes state transition from $t_1$ to $t_2$. Satisfies $\Phi(t;t)=I$, the product rule $\Phi(t;s)\Phi(s;r) = \Phi(t;r)$, and $\Phi^{-1}(t;s) = \Phi(s;t)$.

nodes.name: Random process model (state-space)
nodes.statement: $x(t+1) = \Phi(t+1; t) x(t) + u(t)$, where $\{u(t)\}$ is a vector-valued, independent, gaussian random process with zero mean and $E u(t) u'(s) = 0$ for $t \neq s$, $E u(t) u'(t) = G(t)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Linear Gauss-Markov state-space model driving the observed process.

nodes.name: Innovation $\tilde{y}(t|t-1)$
nodes.statement: The component $\tilde{y}(t|t-1) = y(t) - \bar{y}(t|t-1) = y(t) - M(t) x^*(t|t-1)$ of $y(t)$ orthogonal to $Y(t-1)$, generating the new-information manifold $Z(t)$.
nodes.statement_clean: The orthogonal residual of $y(t)$ relative to past observations; the 'new information' at time $t$.

nodes.name: Conditional expectation operator $\hat{E}$
nodes.statement: $\hat{E}[x(t_1)|Y(t)] \equiv \bar{x}(t_1|t)$, the orthogonal projection of $x(t_1)$ onto $Y(t)$. In the gaussian case it coincides with the conditional expectation $E[x(t_1)|Y(t)]$.

nodes.name: Random process
nodes.statement: A discrete random (stochastic) process is a sequence of random variables $\{x(t)\} = \ldots, x(-1), x(0), x(1), \ldots$ specified by joint distribution functions $F_{x(t_1),\ldots,x(t_n)}(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n) = \Pr[x(t_1) \leq \xi_1,\ldots, x(t_n) \leq \xi_n]$.

nodes.name: Independent / orthogonal / uncorrelated random process
nodes.statement: A process is uncorrelated if $E x(t) x(s) = E x(t) E x(s)$ for $t \neq s$; orthogonal if $E x(t) x(s) = 0$ for $t \neq s$; independent if joint distributions factor as products of first-order distributions.

nodes.name: Gaussian random variable / vector / process
nodes.statement: $x$ is gaussian if $f_x(\xi) = (2\pi E(x-Ex)^2)^{-1/2} \exp(-\frac{1}{2} (\xi - E x)^2 / E(x - Ex)^2)$. A gaussian random vector has density $f_x(\xi) = (2\pi)^{-n/2} (\det C)^{-1/2} \exp(-\frac{1}{2}(\xi - Ex)' C^{-1}(\xi - Ex))$. A gaussian process is one whose finite-dimensional distributions are gaussian.

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (Optimal estimate is conditional expectation)
nodes.statement: Assume $L$ is of type (2) and the conditional distribution function $F(\xi)$ is (A) symmetric about the mean and (B) convex for $\xi \leq \bar{\xi}$. Then the estimator $x_1^*(t_1|t)$ minimizing the average loss is the conditional expectation $x_1^*(t_1|t) = E[x_1(t_1) \mid y(t_0), \ldots, y(t)]$.
assumptions: Conditional distribution $F(\xi)$ is symmetric about its mean
conclusions: $x_1^*(t_1|t) = E[x_1(t_1) \mid y(t_0), \ldots, y(t)]$ minimizes the average loss

nodes.name: Theorem 1-a (Quadratic-loss case)
nodes.statement: If $L(\varepsilon) = \varepsilon^2$, then Theorem 1 holds without assumptions (A) and (B) on $F$; the optimal estimator is again the conditional expectation $E[x_1(t_1)|y(t_0),\ldots,y(t)]$.
conclusions: $x_1^*(t_1|t) = E[x_1(t_1) \mid y(t_0), \ldots, y(t)]$ minimizes the mean-square loss

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1-a
nodes.statement: Expand the conditional expectation $E[(x_1(t_1) - X_1(t_1))^2 | y(t_0), \ldots, y(t)]$ as $E[x_1^2(t_1)|\cdot] - 2 X_1(t_1) E[x_1(t_1)|\cdot] + X_1^2(t_1)$ and differentiate with respect to $X_1(t_1)$; the minimum is at $X_1 = E[x_1|\cdot]$. (Heuristic argument; rigorous version in Doob.)

nodes.name: Theorem 2 (Optimal estimate as orthogonal projection)
nodes.statement: Let $\{x(t)\}, \{y(t)\}$ be random processes with zero mean. If either (A) the processes are gaussian, or (B) the optimal estimate is restricted to be a linear function of the observations and $L(\varepsilon) = \varepsilon^2$, then $x^*(t_1|t) = $ orthogonal projection $\bar{x}(t_1|t)$ of $x(t_1)$ on $Y(t)$.
assumptions: $\{x(t)\}, \{y(t)\}$ are random processes with $E x(t) = E y(t) = 0$
Either (A) processes are gaussian, or (B) estimate is linear in observations and $L(\varepsilon) = \varepsilon^2$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Part (A): direct consequence of the orthogonal-projection minimum-norm property (10). Part (B): $\tilde{x}(t_1|t)$ has zero mean; orthogonal zero-mean random variables are uncorrelated, and gaussian uncorrelated variables are independent (Theorem 5(B)), so $E[\tilde{x}(t_1|t)|y(t_0),\ldots,y(t)] = 0$, giving $E[x(t_1)|\cdot] = \bar{x}(t_1|t)$.

nodes.name: Minimum-norm characterisation
nodes.statement: If $w \in Y(t)$ then $E(x - w)^2 = E(x - \bar{x})^2 + E(\bar{x} - w)^2 \geq E(x - \bar{x})^2$, so $\bar{x}$ minimizes the quadratic loss over $Y(t)$.

nodes.name: Gaussian residual is independent of observations
nodes.statement: $\tilde{x}(t_1|t)$ is orthogonal to $Y(t)$ with zero mean; under gaussianness, orthogonality implies independence (Theorem 5(B)), so $E[\tilde{x}(t_1|t) | y(t_0),\ldots,y(t)] = 0$.

nodes.name: Conclude conditional expectation equals projection
nodes.statement: $0 = E[\tilde{x}(t_1|t) | y(t_0),\ldots,y(t)] = E[x(t_1)|\cdot] - \bar{x}(t_1|t)$, so $E[x(t_1)|y(t_0),\ldots,y(t)] = \bar{x}(t_1|t)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3 (Solution of the Wiener Problem)
nodes.statement: For Problem I, the optimal estimate $x^*(t+1|t)$ is generated by the linear dynamic system $x^*(t+1|t) = \Phi^*(t+1;t) x^*(t|t-1) + \Delta^*(t) y(t)$, with error dynamics $\tilde{x}(t+1|t) = \Phi^*(t+1;t)\tilde{x}(t|t-1) + u(t)$ and error covariance $P^*(t)$ generated by the recursions for $\Delta^*$, $\Phi^*$, $P^*$.
assumptions: Problem I dynamics: $x(t+1) = \Phi(t+1;t) x(t) + u(t)$ with observation $y(t) = M(t) x(t)$
$\{u(t)\}$ independent gaussian with zero mean, covariance $Q(t)$
$P^*(t_0) = E x(t_0) x'(t_0)$ positive definite; $Q(t)$ positive definite; rows of $M(t)$ linearly independent at each $t$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3 (constructive derivation)
nodes.statement: By induction in $t$, decompose $Y(t) = Y(t-1) \oplus Z(t)$ using the innovation, project the state-space update onto these manifolds, identify $\hat{E}[x(t+1)|Z(t)] = \Delta^*(t) \tilde{y}(t|t-1)$, and solve the orthogonality condition $E[x(t+1) - \Delta^* \tilde{y}] \tilde{y}' = 0$ for $\Delta^*$.

nodes.name: Decompose observation manifold
nodes.statement: Define the innovation $\tilde{y}(t|t-1)$, the orthogonal complement of $Y(t-1)$ in $Y(t)$, generating manifold $Z(t)$. Then $Y(t) = Y(t-1) \oplus Z(t)$.

nodes.name: Vanishing of $u$ term for $s \geq 0$
nodes.statement: For $t_1 = t + s$, $s \geq 0$: $u(t_1 - 1)$ is independent of $Y(t-1)$, hence orthogonal to it, so $\hat{E}[u(t_1-1)|Y(t-1)] = 0$.

nodes.name: Linear form on $Z(t)$
nodes.statement: $\hat{E}[x(t+1)|Z(t)] = \Delta^*(t) \tilde{y}(t|t-1)$ for some $n \times p$ matrix $\Delta^*(t)$, since $Z(t)$ is one-dimensional in $\tilde{y}$ direction.

nodes.name: Solve orthogonality for the gain
nodes.statement: From $0 = E[x(t+1) - \Delta^* \tilde{y}] \tilde{y}'(t|t-1)$, after expansion using $\tilde{y} = M \tilde{x} + (\text{noise components})$ and orthogonality of $u(t)$ to $x(t)$, obtain $\Delta^*(t) = \Phi(t+1;t) P^*(t) M'(t) [M(t) P^*(t) M'(t)]^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Derive error recursion and covariance update
nodes.statement: Subtracting state and estimate updates yields $\tilde{x}(t+1|t) = \Phi^*(t+1;t) \tilde{x}(t|t-1) + u(t)$; using independence of $u(t)$ and $\tilde{x}(t|t-1)$ gives $P^*(t+1) = \Phi^*(t+1;t) P^*(t) \Phi'(t+1;t) + Q(t)$.

nodes.name: Riccati-type covariance equation
nodes.statement: Eliminating $\Delta^*$ and $\Phi^*$ from (28-30) gives $P^*(t+1) = \Phi(t+1;t)\{P^*(t) - P^*(t) M'(t) [M(t) P^*(t) M'(t)]^{-1} P^*(t) M(t)\} \Phi'(t+1;t) + Q(t)$ for $t \geq t_0$ (Eq. 32). Plays the role of the Wiener-Hopf equation in this theory.

nodes.name: Kalman filter (recursive optimal estimator)
nodes.statement: Recursive linear estimator that, given the state-space model, propagates the estimate $x^*(t|t-1)$ and error covariance $P^*(t)$ one step at a time using the gain $\Delta^*(t)$.
input: Initial state covariance $P^*(t_0) = E x(t_0) x'(t_0)$
nodes.pseudocode: Initialise: $x^*(t_0|t_0-1) = 0$, $P^*(t_0) = E x(t_0) x'(t_0)$. For $t = t_0, t_0+1, \ldots$: (1) compute gain $\Delta^*(t) = \Phi(t+1;t) P^*(t) M'(t) [M(t) P^*(t) M'(t)]^{-1}$; (2) compute closed-loop transition $\Phi^*(t+1;t) = \Phi(t+1;t) - \Delta^*(t) M(t)$; (3) update estimate $x^*(t+1|t) = \Phi^*(t+1;t) x^*(t|t-1) + \Delta^*(t) y(t)$; (4) update covariance $P^*(t+1) = \Phi^*(t+1;t) P^*(t) \Phi'(t+1;t) + Q(t)$.

nodes.name: Initialize state estimate and covariance
nodes.statement: Set $x^*(t_0|t_0-1) = E x(t_0) = 0$ (zero-mean assumption) and $P^*(t_0) = E x(t_0) x'(t_0)$.

nodes.name: Recursive prediction-update loop
nodes.statement: For each $t = t_0, t_0+1, \ldots$: compute $\Delta^*(t) = \Phi(t+1;t) P^*(t) M'(t) [M(t) P^*(t) M'(t)]^{-1}$; compute $\Phi^*(t+1;t) = \Phi(t+1;t) - \Delta^*(t) M(t)$; update $x^*(t+1|t) = \Phi^*(t+1;t) x^*(t|t-1) + \Delta^*(t) y(t)$ and $P^*(t+1) = \Phi^*(t+1;t) P^*(t) \Phi'(t+1;t) + Q(t)$.

nodes.name: Multistep prediction (optional)
nodes.statement: For $s \geq 1$, output $x^*(t+s|t) = \Phi(t+s; t+1) x^*(t+1|t)$, an explicit propagation of the one-step prediction along the deterministic transition.

nodes.name: Problem II (Noise-free regulator problem)
nodes.statement: Given the deterministic system $x(t+1) = \hat{\Phi}(t+1;t) x(t) + \hat{M}(t) u(t)$ and current state $x(t)$, find a control sequence $u(t), \ldots, u(T)$ minimizing the quadratic performance index $V[x(t)] = \sum_{\tau=t}^{T+1} x'(\tau) \hat{Q}(\tau) x(\tau)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 4 (Duality Theorem)
nodes.statement: Problems I and II are duals: replacing every matrix $X(t) = X(t_0+\tau)$ in the filter recursions (28-30) by $\hat{X}'(t) = \hat{X}'(T - \tau)$ yields the optimal-controller recursions (35-37), and conversely. Time runs forward in filtering and backward in control.
conclusions: Filter equations (28-30) transform into regulator equations (35-37) under matrix-transpose / time-reversal substitution
Both problems reduce to the solution of the Wiener-Hopf-like equation (32)

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4
nodes.statement: Carry out the substitutions in equations (28-30) and (35-37); the correspondence is given in detail in Table 1 of the paper.

nodes.name: Theorem 5 (Properties of Gaussian random processes)
nodes.statement: (A) Linear functions (and conditional expectations) on a gaussian random process are gaussian random variables. (B) Orthogonal gaussian random variables are independent. (C) Given any random process with means $E x(t)$ and covariances $E x(t) x(s)$, there exists a unique gaussian random process with the same means and covariances.
conclusions: (A) Linear/conditional functions of gaussians are gaussian
(C) Existence and uniqueness of a gaussian process with prescribed first and second moments

nodes.name: Example 1 (Signal plus white noise, scalar)
nodes.statement: Model: $x_1(t+1) = \phi_{11} x_1(t) + u_1(t)$, $x_2(t+1) = u_2(t)$, $y_1(t) = x_1(t) + x_2(t)$ with $\phi_{11}$ constant, $E u_1^2 = a^2$, $E u_2^2 = b^2$. Theorem 3 yields $\Delta^*(t) = (\phi_{11} C(t), 0)'$, $\Phi^*(t+1;t)$ as in Eq. (38)-block, and $C(t+1) = 1 - b^2/(a^2 + b^2 + \phi_{11}^2 b^2 C(t))$ with $C(0)=0$, the difference equation playing the role of the Wiener-Hopf equation.

nodes.name: Example 2 (Position-velocity tracking with correlated noise)
nodes.statement: Particles leave origin at $t_0=0$ with random velocity; $x_1(t+1)=x_1(t)+x_2(t)$ (position), $x_2(t+1)=x_2(t)$ (velocity), $x_3(t+1) = \phi_{33} x_3(t) + u_3(t)$ (correlated noise), $y_1(t)=x_1(t)+x_3(t)$. Closed-form covariance involves $C_1(t) = C_1(t-1) + (t - \phi_{33}(t-1))^2$ with $C_1(0) = b^2/a^2$. As $t \to \infty$, $C_1(t) \sim (1-\phi_{33})^2 t^3/3$; for $\phi_{33}=0$ recovers Shinbrot/Solodovnikov result $E \tilde{x}_1^2(t|t) \approx a^2 b^2 t^2 / (b^2 + a^2 t^3/3)$.

nodes.name: Innovation is white noise
nodes.statement: Inspection of the optimal filter shows it is a feedback system whose post-summer signal $\tilde{y}(t|t-1)$ is white noise (an orthogonal random process). This realises every Wiener filter as a feedback system, a result that is rigorous here for the first time.

nodes.name: Recovery of the differential-equation filter
nodes.statement: Letting the sampling period approach zero recovers a differential-equation specification of the optimal filter; this requires modifications since $\Phi^*$ is generally singular and only $n - p$ state variables are needed.

nodes.name: Nonstationarity and growing memory
nodes.statement: The derivations are unaffected by nonstationarity of the model for $x(t)$ or finiteness of available data; the only prior explicit growing-memory recursions are due to Blum [12], and are more complicated.
